questions.text:
Let $A=\{(x, y)\in\mathbf{R}\times\mathbf{R}:|x+y|\geq3\}$ and $B=\{(x, y)\in\mathbf{R}\times\mathbf{R}:|x|+|y|\leq3\}$.
If $C=\{(x, y)\in A\cap B: x=0$ or $y=0\}$, then $\displaystyle\sum_{(x, y)\in C}|x+y|$ is :
questions.sol:
On $x=0$: $|y|\ge3$ and $|y|\le3$, so $y=\pm3$. On $y=0$: likewise $x=\pm3$.
$C=\{(0,3),(0,-3),(3,0),(-3,0)\}$, and each point has $|x+y|=3$.
Sum $=4\times3=12$.

questions.text:
Let $X=\mathbf{R}\times\mathbf{R}$. Define a relation R on X as :
$(a_1, b_1)\,R\,(a_2, b_2)\Leftrightarrow b_1=b_2$.
Statement I : R is an equivalence relation.
Statement II : For some $(a, b)\in X$, the set $S=\{(x, y)\in X:(x, y)\,R\,(a, b)\}$ represents a line parallel to $y=x$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
"Same second coordinate" is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, so R is an equivalence relation: Statement I is true.
$S=\{(x,y): y=b\}$ is the horizontal line $y=b$, which is parallel to the $x$-axis, never to $y=x$: Statement II is false.

questions.text: The number of complex numbers $z$, satisfying $|z|=1$ and $\left|\dfrac{z}{\bar z}+\dfrac{\bar z}{z}\right|=1$, is :
questions.sol:
Write $z=e^{i\theta}$. Then $\dfrac{z}{\bar z}+\dfrac{\bar z}{z}=e^{2i\theta}+e^{-2i\theta}=2\cos2\theta$.
$|2\cos2\theta|=1 \Rightarrow \cos2\theta=\pm\dfrac12$.
For $\theta\in[0,2\pi)$, $2\theta\in[0,4\pi)$, and each of $\cos2\theta=\dfrac12$ and $\cos2\theta=-\dfrac12$ has 4 solutions.
Number of $z$ $=8$.

questions.text:
The system of equations
$x+y+z=6,$
$x+2y+5z=9,$
$x+5y+\lambda z=\mu,$
has no solution if
questions.sol:
$\Delta=\begin{vmatrix}1&1&1\\1&2&5\\1&5&\lambda\end{vmatrix}=(2\lambda-25)-(\lambda-5)+3=\lambda-17$, so no unique solution needs $\lambda=17$.
With $\lambda=17$: $(1,5,17)=-3(1,1,1)+4(1,2,5)$, so the third equation is consistent only if $\mu=-3(6)+4(9)=18$.
No solution when $\lambda=17,\ \mu\neq18$.

questions.text: Let $A=[a_{ij}]$ be a $3\times3$ matrix such that $A\begin{bmatrix}0\\1\\0\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0\\0\\1\end{bmatrix}$, $A\begin{bmatrix}4\\1\\3\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0\\1\\0\end{bmatrix}$ and $A\begin{bmatrix}2\\1\\2\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1\\0\\0\end{bmatrix}$, then $a_{23}$ equals :
questions.sol:
Let $c_1,c_2,c_3$ be the columns of $A$ and $e_1,e_2,e_3$ the unit vectors. Then $c_2=e_3$.
$4c_1+c_2+3c_3=e_2$ and $2c_1+c_2+2c_3=e_1$.
Subtracting: $2c_1+c_3=e_2-e_1$. The second equation gives $2c_1+2c_3=e_1-e_3$.
So $c_3=(e_1-e_3)-(e_2-e_1)=2e_1-e_2-e_3=(2,-1,-1)^T$.
$a_{23}$ is the second entry of $c_3$: $a_{23}=-1$.

questions.text: If in the expansion of $(1+x)^p(1-x)^q$, the coefficients of $x$ and $x^2$ are 1 and $-2$, respectively, then $p^2+q^2$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Coefficient of $x$: $p-q=1$.
Coefficient of $x^2$: $\dbinom p2+\dbinom q2-pq=\dfrac{(p-q)^2-(p+q)}{2}=\dfrac{1-(p+q)}{2}=-2$, so $p+q=5$.
$p=3$, $q=2$, and $p^2+q^2=13$.

questions.text:
A board has 16 squares as shown in the figure :
Out of these 16 squares, two squares are chosen at random. The probability that they have no side in common is :
questions.sol:
Number of ways to choose 2 squares $=\dbinom{16}{2}=120$.
Pairs sharing a side: each of the 4 rows has 3 adjacent pairs and so does each of the 4 columns, giving $24$.
Probability $=\dfrac{120-24}{120}=\dfrac{96}{120}=\dfrac45$.

questions.text: The length of the chord of the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{4}+\dfrac{y^2}{2}=1$, whose mid-point is $\left(1,\dfrac12\right)$, is :
questions.sol:
Chord with given mid-point: $T=S_1$, i.e. $\dfrac{x}{4}+\dfrac{y}{4}=\dfrac14+\dfrac18$, so $x+y=\dfrac32$.
Substituting $y=\dfrac32-x$: $x^2+2\left(\dfrac32-x\right)^2=4 \Rightarrow 6x^2-12x+1=0$.
$|x_1-x_2|=\dfrac{\sqrt{144-24}}{6}=\dfrac{\sqrt{120}}{6}$; the chord has slope $-1$, so its length is $\sqrt2\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt{120}}{6}=\dfrac{4\sqrt{15}}{6}=\dfrac23\sqrt{15}$.

questions.text: Let the shortest distance from $(a, 0)$, $a>0$, to the parabola $y^2=4x$ be 4. Then the equation of the circle passing through the point $(a, 0)$ and the focus of the parabola, and having its centre on the axis of the parabola is :
questions.sol:
The shortest distance is along a normal. The normal at $(t^2,2t)$ is $y=-tx+2t+t^3$; through $(a,0)$: $a=2+t^2$.
Distance$^2=(a-t^2)^2+4t^2=4+4t^2=16 \Rightarrow t^2=3$, $a=5$.
The circle has its centre on the $x$-axis and passes through $(5,0)$ and the focus $(1,0)$, so its centre is $(3,0)$ and radius 2.
$(x-3)^2+y^2=4$, i.e. $x^2+y^2-6x+5=0$.

questions.text: Let the range of the function $f(x)=6+16\cos x\cdot\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}-x\right)\cdot\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}+x\right)\cdot\sin3x\cdot\cos6x$, $x\in\mathbf{R}$ be $[\alpha, \beta]$. Then the distance of the point $(\alpha, \beta)$ from the line $3x+4y+12=0$ is :
questions.sol:
$\cos x\cos\left(\dfrac\pi3-x\right)\cos\left(\dfrac\pi3+x\right)=\dfrac{\cos3x}{4}$.
So $f(x)=6+4\sin3x\cos3x\cos6x=6+2\sin6x\cos6x=6+\sin12x$, with range $[5,7]$.
Distance of $(5,7)$ from $3x+4y+12=0$: $\dfrac{|15+28+12|}{5}=11$.

questions.text: The distance of the line $\dfrac{x-2}{2}=\dfrac{y-6}{3}=\dfrac{z-3}{4}$ from the point $(1, 4, 0)$ along the line $\dfrac{x}{1}=\dfrac{y-2}{2}=\dfrac{z+3}{3}$ is :
questions.sol:
Move from $(1,4,0)$ in the direction $(1,2,3)$: $(1+t,\,4+2t,\,3t)$.
On the first line: $1+t=2+2s$, $4+2t=6+3s$, $3t=3+4s$. The first two give $s=0$, $t=1$, and the third checks.
Meeting point $(2,6,3)$; distance $=\sqrt{1^2+2^2+3^2}=\sqrt{14}$.

questions.text: If the square of the shortest distance between the lines $\dfrac{x-2}{1}=\dfrac{y-1}{2}=\dfrac{z+3}{-3}$ and $\dfrac{x+1}{2}=\dfrac{y+3}{4}=\dfrac{z+5}{-5}$ is $\dfrac{m}{n}$, where m, n are coprime numbers, then $m+n$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Points $(2,1,-3)$ and $(-1,-3,-5)$; directions $(1,2,-3)$ and $(2,4,-5)$.
$(1,2,-3)\times(2,4,-5)=(2,-1,0)$, of length $\sqrt5$.
Joining vector $(-3,-4,-2)$; its dot product with $(2,-1,0)$ is $-6+4=-2$.
Shortest distance $=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt5}$, square $=\dfrac45$, so $m+n=9$.

questions.text: $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{(2x^2-3x+5)(3x-1)^{\frac{x}{2}}}{(3x^2+5x+4)\sqrt{(3x+2)^x}}$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{2x^2-3x+5}{3x^2+5x+4}\to\dfrac23$.
$\dfrac{(3x-1)^{x/2}}{(3x+2)^{x/2}}=\left(1-\dfrac{3}{3x+2}\right)^{x/2}\to e^{\lim\left(-\frac{3}{3x+2}\cdot\frac x2\right)}=e^{-1/2}$.
Limit $=\dfrac{2}{3\sqrt e}$.

questions.text: A spherical chocolate ball has a layer of ice-cream of uniform thickness around it. When the thickness of the ice-cream layer is 1 cm, the ice-cream melts at the rate of 81 cm$^3$/min and the thickness of the ice-cream layer decreases at the rate of $\dfrac{1}{4\pi}$ cm/min. The surface area (in cm$^2$) of the chocolate ball (without the ice-cream layer) is :
questions.sol:
Let the ball have radius $r$ and the layer thickness $h$. The ice-cream volume is $\dfrac43\pi(r+h)^3-\dfrac43\pi r^3$, so $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=4\pi(r+h)^2\dfrac{dh}{dt}$.
$81=4\pi(r+1)^2\cdot\dfrac{1}{4\pi} \Rightarrow (r+1)^2=81 \Rightarrow r=8$.
Surface area $=4\pi r^2=256\pi$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If the area of the region $\{(x, y):-1\leq x\leq1,\ 0\leq y\leq a+e^{|x|}-e^{-x},\ a>0\}$ is $\dfrac{e^2+8e+1}{e}$, then the value of a is :
questions.sol:
The upper boundary is non-negative ($=a$ for $x\le0$ and $>a$ for $x>0$).
Area $=\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1}\left(a+e^{|x|}-e^{-x}\right)dx=2a+2(e-1)-\left(e-\frac1e\right)=2a+e-2+\frac1e$.
Setting this equal to $e+8+\dfrac1e$ gives $2a=10$, $a=5$.

questions.text: Let $\displaystyle\int x^3\sin x\,dx=g(x)+C$, where C is the constant of integration. If $8\left(g\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)+g'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\right)=\alpha\pi^3+\beta\pi^2+\gamma$, $\alpha, \beta, \gamma\in\mathbf{Z}$, then $\alpha+\beta-\gamma$ equals :
questions.sol:
By parts repeatedly: $g(x)=-x^3\cos x+3x^2\sin x+6x\cos x-6\sin x$, and $g'(x)=x^3\sin x$.
$g\left(\dfrac\pi2\right)=\dfrac{3\pi^2}{4}-6$, $g'\left(\dfrac\pi2\right)=\dfrac{\pi^3}{8}$.
$8(g+g')=\pi^3+6\pi^2-48$, so $\alpha=1$, $\beta=6$, $\gamma=-48$.
$\alpha+\beta-\gamma=55$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If $I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{\sin^{\frac32}x}{\sin^{\frac32}x+\cos^{\frac32}x}\,dx$, then $\displaystyle\int_0^{2I}\frac{x\sin x\cos x}{\sin^4x+\cos^4x}\,dx$ equals :
questions.sol:
Replacing $x$ by $\dfrac\pi2-x$ and adding gives $2I=\dfrac\pi2$.
For $J=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{x\sin x\cos x}{\sin^4x+\cos^4x}dx$, the same substitution gives $J=\dfrac\pi4\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{\sin x\cos x}{\sin^4x+\cos^4x}dx$.
Put $t=\sin^2x$: $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{\sin x\cos x}{\sin^4x+\cos^4x}dx=\frac12\int_0^1\frac{dt}{t^2+(1-t)^2}=\frac12\int_0^1\frac{dt}{2t^2-2t+1}=\frac12\left[\tan^{-1}(2t-1)\right]_0^1=\frac\pi4$.
$J=\dfrac\pi4\cdot\dfrac\pi4=\dfrac{\pi^2}{16}$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $x=x(y)$ be the solution of the differential equation $y=\left(x-y\dfrac{dx}{dy}\right)\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right)$, $y>0$ and $x(1)=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$. Then $\cos(x(2))$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Put $x=vy$: $\dfrac{dx}{dy}=v+y\dfrac{dv}{dy}$, so $x-y\dfrac{dx}{dy}=-y^2\dfrac{dv}{dy}$.
The equation becomes $y=-y^2\sin v\dfrac{dv}{dy}$, i.e. $\sin v\,dv=-\dfrac{dy}{y}$, so $\cos v=\log_e y+c$.
At $y=1$, $v=\dfrac\pi2$: $c=0$. Hence $\cos\dfrac{x}{y}=\log_e y$.
At $y=2$: $\cos\dfrac{x(2)}{2}=\log_e2$, so $\cos(x(2))=2\cos^2\dfrac{x(2)}{2}-1=2(\log_e2)^2-1$.

questions.text: Let the point A divide the line segment joining the points $P(-1, -1, 2)$ and $Q(5, 5, 10)$ internally in the ratio $r:1$ $(r>0)$. If O is the origin and $\left(\overrightarrow{OQ}\cdot\overrightarrow{OA}\right)-\dfrac15\left|\overrightarrow{OP}\times\overrightarrow{OA}\right|^2=10$, then the value of r is :
questions.sol:
$\overrightarrow{OA}=\dfrac{r\overrightarrow{OQ}+\overrightarrow{OP}}{r+1}=\dfrac{(5r-1,\,5r-1,\,10r+2)}{r+1}$.
$\overrightarrow{OQ}\cdot\overrightarrow{OA}=\dfrac{150r+10}{r+1}$.
$\overrightarrow{OP}\times\overrightarrow{OA}=\dfrac{r}{r+1}\,\overrightarrow{OP}\times\overrightarrow{OQ}=\dfrac{r}{r+1}(-20,20,0)$, so $\left|\overrightarrow{OP}\times\overrightarrow{OA}\right|^2=\dfrac{800r^2}{(r+1)^2}$.
$(150r+10)(r+1)-160r^2=10(r+1)^2 \Rightarrow 20r^2=140r \Rightarrow r=7$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The roots of the quadratic equation $3x^2-px+q=0$ are $10^{\text{th}}$ and $11^{\text{th}}$ terms of an arithmetic progression with common difference $\dfrac32$. If the sum of the first 11 terms of this arithmetic progression is 88, then $q-2p$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
$S_{11}=11a_6=88 \Rightarrow a_6=8$. Then $a_{10}=8+4\cdot\dfrac32=14$ and $a_{11}=\dfrac{31}{2}$.
Sum of roots $=\dfrac p3=\dfrac{59}{2} \Rightarrow p=\dfrac{177}{2}$; product $=\dfrac q3=217 \Rightarrow q=651$.
$q-2p=651-177=474$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $\alpha, \beta$ be the roots of the equation $x^2-ax-b=0$ with $\mathrm{Im}(\alpha)<\mathrm{Im}(\beta)$. Let $P_n=\alpha^n-\beta^n$. If $P_3=-5\sqrt7\,i$, $P_4=-3\sqrt7\,i$, $P_5=11\sqrt7\,i$ and $P_6=45\sqrt7\,i$, then $|\alpha^4+\beta^4|$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Since $\alpha^2=a\alpha+b$ and $\beta^2=a\beta+b$, $P_{n+1}=aP_n+bP_{n-1}$.
$P_5=aP_4+bP_3$: $11=-3a-5b$. $P_6=aP_5+bP_4$: $45=11a-3b$.
Solving: $a=3$, $b=-4$, so $\alpha+\beta=3$ and $\alpha\beta=4$.
$\alpha^2+\beta^2=9-8=1$, $\alpha^4+\beta^4=1-2(16)=-31$, so $|\alpha^4+\beta^4|=31$.

questions.text: The number of ways, 5 boys and 4 girls can sit in a row so that either all the boys sit together or no two boys sit together, is __________.
questions.sol:
All boys together: treat the boys as one block with the 4 girls, $5!$ ways, times $5!$ inside the block: $14400$.
No two boys together: arrange the girls in $4!$ ways; the 5 gaps take the 5 boys in $5!$ ways: $2880$.
The two cases cannot happen together, so the total is $14400+2880=17280$.

questions.text: The variance of the numbers 8, 21, 34, 47, ..., 320 is __________.
questions.sol:
This is an A.P. with $d=13$: $8+13(n-1)=320 \Rightarrow n=25$.
For $n$ terms of an A.P., variance $=\dfrac{d^2(n^2-1)}{12}=\dfrac{169\times624}{12}=169\times52=8788$.

questions.text: The focus of the parabola $y^2=4x+16$ is the centre of the circle C of radius 5. If the values of $\lambda$, for which C passes through the point of intersection of the lines $3x-y=0$ and $x+\lambda y=4$, are $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$, $\lambda_1<\lambda_2$, then $12\lambda_1+29\lambda_2$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
$y^2=4(x+4)$ has focus $(-3,0)$, so C is $(x+3)^2+y^2=25$.
The lines meet at $x=4u$, $y=12u$ with $u=\dfrac{1}{1+3\lambda}$.
$(4u+3)^2+144u^2=25 \Rightarrow 20u^2+3u-2=0 \Rightarrow u=\dfrac14$ or $-\dfrac25$.
$1+3\lambda=4 \Rightarrow \lambda=1$; $1+3\lambda=-\dfrac52 \Rightarrow \lambda=-\dfrac76$.
$12\lambda_1+29\lambda_2=12\left(-\dfrac76\right)+29(1)=15$.

questions.text: The energy of a system is given as $E(t)=\alpha^3e^{-\beta t}$, where t is the time and $\beta=0.3$ s$^{-1}$. The errors in the measurement of $\alpha$ and t are 1.2% and 1.6%, respectively. At $t=5$ s, maximum percentage error in the energy is :
questions.sol:
$\ln E=3\ln\alpha-\beta t$, so $\dfrac{\Delta E}{E}=3\dfrac{\Delta\alpha}{\alpha}+\beta t\dfrac{\Delta t}{t}$.
$=3(1.2\%)+(0.3)(5)(1.6\%)=3.6\%+2.4\%=6\%$.

questions.text: A ball having kinetic energy KE, is projected at an angle of $60^\circ$ from the horizontal. What will be the kinetic energy of ball at the highest point of its flight ?
questions.sol:
At the highest point only the horizontal component $u\cos60^\circ=\dfrac u2$ remains.
KE there $=\dfrac12m\left(\dfrac u2\right)^2=\dfrac{KE}{4}$.

questions.text:
A circular disk of radius R meter and mass M kg is rotating around the axis perpendicular to the disk. An external torque is applied to the disk such that $\theta(t)=5t^2-8t$, where $\theta(t)$ is the angular position of the rotating disc as a function of time t.
How much power is delivered by the applied torque, when $t=2$ s ?
questions.sol:
$\omega=\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}=10t-8=12$ rad/s at $t=2$ s, and $\alpha=10$ rad/s$^2$.
Taking the axis through the centre, $I=\dfrac{MR^2}{2}$, so $\tau=I\alpha=5MR^2$.
Power $=\tau\omega=60\,MR^2$.

questions.text: If a satellite orbiting the Earth is 9 times closer to the Earth than the Moon, what is the time period of rotation of the satellite? Given rotational time period of Moon $=27$ days and gravitational attraction between the satellite and the moon is neglected.
questions.sol:
Kepler's third law: $T\propto r^{3/2}$.
$T_s=27\times\left(\dfrac19\right)^{3/2}=\dfrac{27}{27}=1$ day.

questions.text: A massless spring gets elongated by amount $x_1$ under a tension of 5 N. Its elongation is $x_2$ under the tension of 7 N. For the elongation of $(5x_1-2x_2)$, the tension in the spring will be,
questions.sol:
With $F=kx$: $x_1=\dfrac5k$, $x_2=\dfrac7k$.
$5x_1-2x_2=\dfrac{25-14}{k}=\dfrac{11}{k}$, so the tension is $11$ N.

questions.text: Water flows in a horizontal pipe whose one end is closed with a valve. The reading of the pressure gauge attached to the pipe is $P_1$. The reading of the pressure gauge falls to $P_2$ when the valve is opened. The speed of water flowing in the pipe is proportional to
questions.sol:
Bernoulli's equation for the horizontal pipe: $P_1=P_2+\dfrac12\rho v^2$.
$v=\sqrt{\dfrac{2(P_1-P_2)}{\rho}}\propto\sqrt{P_1-P_2}$.

questions.text: Using the given P-V diagram, the work done by an ideal gas along the path ABCD is :
questions.sol:
A to B at $P_0$ from $2V_0$ to $3V_0$: $W=P_0V_0$.
B to C at constant volume: $W=0$.
C to D at $2P_0$ from $3V_0$ to $V_0$: $W=2P_0(-2V_0)=-4P_0V_0$.
Total $=-3P_0V_0$.

questions.text: Water of mass m gram is slowly heated to increase the temperature from $T_1$ to $T_2$. The change in entropy of the water, given specific heat of water is 1 Jkg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$, is :
questions.sol:
For slow (reversible) heating, $dS=\dfrac{dQ}{T}=\dfrac{mc\,dT}{T}$.
$\Delta S=mc\displaystyle\int_{T_1}^{T_2}\frac{dT}{T}=mc\ln\frac{T_2}{T_1}$, which is $m\ln\dfrac{T_2}{T_1}$ with $c=1$ (taking $m$ in the unit that matches $c$).

questions.text:
The equation of a transverse wave travelling along a string is
$y(x, t)=4.0\sin[20\times10^{-3}x+600t]$mm, where $x$ is in mm and $t$ is in second. The velocity of the wave is :
questions.sol:
For $\sin(kx+\omega t)$ the disturbance moves in the $-x$ direction with speed $\dfrac\omega k$.
$\dfrac{\omega}{k}=\dfrac{600}{20\times10^{-3}}=3\times10^4$ mm/s $=30$ m/s.
Velocity $=-30$ m/s.

questions.text: Two point charges $-4\ \mu$c and $4\ \mu$c, constituting an electric dipole, are placed at $(-9, 0, 0)$ cm and $(9, 0, 0)$ cm in a uniform electric field of strength $10^4$ N C$^{-1}$. The work done on the dipole in rotating it from the equilibrium through $180^\circ$ is :
questions.sol:
Dipole moment $p=q(2a)=4\times10^{-6}\times0.18=7.2\times10^{-7}$ C m.
From stable equilibrium through $180^\circ$: $W=pE(\cos0^\circ-\cos180^\circ)=2pE$.
$W=2\times7.2\times10^{-7}\times10^4=1.44\times10^{-2}$ J $=14.4$ mJ.

questions.text: Two charges $7\ \mu$c and $-4\ \mu$c are placed at $(-7$ cm, 0, 0) and (7 cm, 0, 0) respectively. Given, $\epsilon_0=8.85\times10^{-12}$ C$^2$ N$^{-1}$ m$^{-2}$, the electrostatic potential energy of the charge configuration is :

questions.text: A plane electromagnetic wave of frequency 20 MHz travels in free space along the $+x$ direction. At a particular point in space and time, the electric field vector of the wave is $E_y=9.3$ Vm$^{-1}$. Then, the magnetic field vector of the wave at that point is
questions.sol:
$B=\dfrac Ec=\dfrac{9.3}{3\times10^8}=3.1\times10^{-8}$ T.
$\vec E\times\vec B$ must point along $+x$; with $\vec E$ along $\hat y$, $\vec B$ is along $\hat z$ (since $\hat y\times\hat z=\hat x$).

questions.text: The refractive index of the material of a glass prism is $\sqrt3$. The angle of minimum deviation is equal to the angle of the prism. What is the angle of the prism ?
questions.sol:
$\mu=\dfrac{\sin\frac{A+\delta_m}{2}}{\sin\frac A2}$ with $\delta_m=A$: $\mu=\dfrac{\sin A}{\sin\frac A2}=2\cos\dfrac A2$.
$2\cos\dfrac A2=\sqrt3 \Rightarrow \dfrac A2=30^\circ$, $A=60^\circ$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The width of one of the two slits in Young's double slit experiment is d while that of the other slit is $x$d. If the ratio of the maximum to the minimum intensity in the interference pattern on the screen is $9:4$ then what is the value of $x$ ?
(Assume that the field strength varies according to the slit width.)
questions.sol:
The field amplitudes are in the ratio $1:x$.
$\dfrac{I_{\max}}{I_{\min}}=\left(\dfrac{x+1}{x-1}\right)^2=\dfrac94 \Rightarrow \dfrac{x+1}{x-1}=\dfrac32 \Rightarrow x=5$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A concave mirror of focal length $f$ in air is dipped in a liquid of refractive index $\mu$. Its focal length in the liquid will be :
questions.sol:
For a mirror, $f=\dfrac R2$ depends only on the curvature; reflection does not depend on the surrounding medium.
The focal length stays $f$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
In photoelectric effect an em-wave is incident on a metal surface and electrons are ejected from the surface. If the work function of the metal is 2.14 eV and stopping potential is 2V, what is the wavelength of the em-wave ?
(Given $hc=1242$ eVnm where h is the Planck's constant and c is the speed of light in vaccum.)
questions.sol:
Photon energy $=\phi+eV_0=2.14+2=4.14$ eV.
$\lambda=\dfrac{1242}{4.14}=300$ nm.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text:
Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : The binding energy per nucleon is found to be practically independent of the atomic number A, for nuclei with mass numbers between 30 and 170.
Reason (R) : Nuclear force is long range.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.sol:
The binding energy per nucleon is nearly constant (about 8 MeV) for mass numbers 30 to 170, so (A) is true.
This saturation happens because the nuclear force is short range, so (R) is false.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: What is the current through the battery in the circuit shown below ?
questions.sol:
Both diodes point the same way and are forward biased by the battery, so (treating them as ideal) both branches conduct.
Two 20 $\Omega$ branches in parallel give 10 $\Omega$.
$I=\dfrac{5}{10}=0.5$ A.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A satellite of mass $\dfrac{M}{2}$ is revolving around earth in a circular orbit at a height of $\dfrac{R}{3}$ from earth surface. The angular momentum of the satellite is $M\sqrt{\dfrac{GMR}{x}}$. The value of $x$ is __________, where M and R are the mass and radius of earth, respectively.
(G is the gravitational constant)
questions.sol:
Orbit radius $r=R+\dfrac R3=\dfrac{4R}{3}$ and orbital speed $v=\sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{r}}$.
$L=mvr=\dfrac M2\sqrt{GMr}=\dfrac M2\sqrt{\dfrac{4GMR}{3}}=M\sqrt{\dfrac{GMR}{3}}$.
$x=3$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
An air bubble of radius 1.0 mm is observed at a depth of 20 cm below the free surface of a liquid having surface tension 0.095 J/m$^2$ and density $10^3$ kg/m$^3$. The difference between pressure inside the bubble and atmospheric pressure is __________ N/m$^2$.
(Take $g=10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.sol:
Inside an air bubble in a liquid (one surface): $P_{\text{in}}=P_0+\rho gh+\dfrac{2T}{r}$.
$\rho gh=10^3\times10\times0.2=2000$ N/m$^2$; $\dfrac{2T}{r}=\dfrac{2\times0.095}{10^{-3}}=190$ N/m$^2$.
Difference $=2190$ N/m$^2$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A time varying potential difference is applied between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor of capacitance 2.5 $\mu$F. The dielectric constant of the medium between the capacitor plates is 1. It produces an instantaneous displacement current of 0.25 mA in the intervening space between the capacitor plates, the magnitude of the rate of change of the potential difference will be __________ Vs$^{-1}$.
questions.sol:
Displacement current $I_d=\epsilon_0\dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}=C\dfrac{dV}{dt}$.
$\dfrac{dV}{dt}=\dfrac{0.25\times10^{-3}}{2.5\times10^{-6}}=100$ V s$^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In a series LCR circuit, a resistor of 300 $\Omega$, a capacitor of 25 nF and an inductor of 100 mH are used. For maximum current in the circuit, the angular frequency of the ac source is __________ $\times10^4$ radians s$^{-1}$.
questions.sol:
Maximum current at resonance: $\omega=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$.
$LC=0.1\times25\times10^{-9}=2.5\times10^{-9}$ s$^2$, $\sqrt{LC}=5\times10^{-5}$ s.
$\omega=2\times10^4$ rad s$^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: At steady state the charge on the capacitor, as shown in the circuit below, is __________ $\mu$C.
questions.sol:
At steady state no current flows through the capacitor branch, so the current is $\dfrac{5}{10+15}=0.2$ A.
The capacitor is in parallel with the 10 $\Omega$ resistor: $V=0.2\times10=2$ V.
$Q=CV=8\times2=16\ \mu$C.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : For a given shell, the total number of allowed orbitals is given by $n^2$.
Statement (II) : For any subshell, the spatial orientation of the orbitals is given by $-l$ to $+l$ values including zero.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Shell $n$ has subshells $l=0$ to $n-1$ with $2l+1$ orbitals each: total $\sum(2l+1)=n^2$. Statement I is true.
The orientation of the orbitals is given by $m_l=-l,\ldots,0,\ldots,+l$. Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The effect of temperature on spontaneity of reactions are represented as :
$\Delta H$$\Delta S$TemperatureSpontaneity
(A)+$-$any TNon spontaneous
(B)++low Tspontaneous
(C)$-$$-$low TNon spontaneous
(D)$-$+any Tspontaneous
The incorrect combinations are :
questions.sol:
Use $\Delta G=\Delta H-T\Delta S$.
(A) $\Delta H>0$, $\Delta S<0$: $\Delta G>0$ always, non-spontaneous: correct.
(B) $\Delta H>0$, $\Delta S>0$: spontaneous only at high T, so "spontaneous at low T" is incorrect.
(C) $\Delta H<0$, $\Delta S<0$: spontaneous at low T, so "non-spontaneous at low T" is incorrect.
(D) $\Delta H<0$, $\Delta S>0$: always spontaneous: correct.
Incorrect: (B) and (C).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Standard electrode potentials for a few half cells are mentioned below :
$E^\circ_{\mathrm{Cu^{2+}/Cu}}=0.34$ V, $E^\circ_{\mathrm{Zn^{2+}/Zn}}=-0.76$ V
$E^\circ_{\mathrm{Ag^+/Ag}}=0.80$ V, $E^\circ_{\mathrm{Mg^{2+}/Mg}}=-2.37$ V
Which one of the following cells gives the most negative value of $\Delta G^\circ$ ?
questions.sol:
$\Delta G^\circ=-nFE^\circ_{\text{cell}}$ with $E^\circ_{\text{cell}}=E^\circ_{\text{right}}-E^\circ_{\text{left}}$; per mole of reaction written with $n=2$:
Zn/Mg: $-2.37-(-0.76)=-1.61$ V (positive $\Delta G^\circ$).
Cu/Ag: $0.80-0.34=0.46$ V.
Zn/Ag: $0.80-(-0.76)=1.56$ V.
Ag/Mg: $-2.37-0.80=-3.17$ V (positive $\Delta G^\circ$).
The largest positive $E^\circ_{\text{cell}}$, hence the most negative $\Delta G^\circ$, is for $\mathrm{Zn|Zn^{2+}||Ag^+|Ag}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: When a non-volatile solute is added to the solvent, the vapour pressure of the solvent decreases by 10 mm of Hg. The mole fraction of the solute in the solution is 0.2. What would be the mole fraction of the solvent if decrease in vapour pressure is 20 mm of Hg ?
questions.sol:
Raoult's law: $\dfrac{\Delta p}{p^\circ}=x_{\text{solute}}$, so $\dfrac{10}{p^\circ}=0.2 \Rightarrow p^\circ=50$ mm Hg.
For $\Delta p=20$: $x_{\text{solute}}=\dfrac{20}{50}=0.4$, so $x_{\text{solvent}}=0.6$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Consider a binary solution of two volatile liquid components 1 and 2. $x_1$ and $y_1$ are the mole fractions of component 1 in liquid and vapour phase, respectively. The slope and intercept of the linear plot of $\dfrac{1}{x_1}$ vs $\dfrac{1}{y_1}$ are given respectively as :
questions.sol:
$y_1=\dfrac{x_1P_1^0}{P}$ with $P=P_2^0+x_1(P_1^0-P_2^0)$.
So $\dfrac{1}{y_1}=\dfrac{P_2^0}{P_1^0}\cdot\dfrac{1}{x_1}+\dfrac{P_1^0-P_2^0}{P_1^0}$.
Rearranged with $\dfrac1{x_1}$ as the dependent variable: $\dfrac{1}{x_1}=\dfrac{P_1^0}{P_2^0}\cdot\dfrac{1}{y_1}+\dfrac{P_2^0-P_1^0}{P_2^0}$.
Slope $\dfrac{P_1^0}{P_2^0}$, intercept $\dfrac{P_2^0-P_1^0}{P_2^0}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the reaction
$\mathrm{X_2Y(g)\rightleftharpoons X_2(g)+\dfrac12Y_2(g)}$
The equation representing correct relationship between the degree of dissociation $(x)$ of $\mathrm{X_2Y(g)}$ with its equilibrium constant Kp is __________.
Assume $x$ to be very very small.
questions.sol:
Moles at equilibrium: $1-x$, $x$, $\dfrac x2$; total $1+\dfrac x2\approx1$ for small $x$.
$K_p=\dfrac{(xp)\left(\frac x2p\right)^{1/2}}{(1-x)p}\approx\dfrac{x^{3/2}p^{1/2}}{\sqrt2}$.
$x^{3/2}=\dfrac{\sqrt2K_p}{\sqrt p} \Rightarrow x^3=\dfrac{2K_p^2}{p} \Rightarrow x=\sqrt[3]{\dfrac{2K_p^2}{p}}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which of the following graphs most appropriately represents a zero order reaction ?
questions.sol:
For a zero order reaction, rate $=k$ is constant and $[\mathrm{R}]=[\mathrm{R}]_0-kt$.
So reactant concentration falls linearly with time: the straight line with negative slope on the concentration-time graph.
The two rate-time graphs show a falling rate, and the flat concentration line shows no reaction.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: pH of water is 7 at 25$^\circ$C. If water is heated to 80$^\circ$C., it's pH will :
questions.sol:
Self-ionisation of water is endothermic, so $K_w$ increases on heating.
$[\mathrm{H^+}]=[\mathrm{OH^-}]=\sqrt{K_w}$ both increase (water stays neutral), so the pH falls below 7.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements about X-ray spectra of elements :
Statement (I) : A plot of $\sqrt{ u}$ ($ u=$ frequency of X-rays emitted) vs atomic mass is a straight line.
Statement (II) : A plot of $ u$ ($ u=$ frequency of X-rays emitted) vs atomic number is a straight line.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Moseley found that $\sqrt u$ plotted against atomic number $Z$ is a straight line.
Statement I uses atomic mass, so it is false. Statement II plots $ u$ (not $\sqrt u$) against $Z$, which is a curve, so it is false.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text: Given below are the atomic numbers of some group 14 elements. The atomic number of the element with lowest melting point is :
questions.sol:
The numbers are C (6), Si (14), Sn (50) and Pb (82).
Melting points: C and Si are very high (network solids); Pb about 600 K; Sn about 505 K.
Tin has the lowest melting point: atomic number 50.

questions.text:
Consider the following reactions
$\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7\xrightarrow[-H_2O]{KOH}[A]\xrightarrow[-H_2O]{H_2SO_4}[B]+K_2SO_4}$
The products [A] and [B], respectively are :
questions.sol:
In alkali, dichromate changes to chromate: $\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7+2KOH\rightarrow2K_2CrO_4+H_2O}$, so A is $\mathrm{K_2CrO_4}$.
In acid, chromate changes back: $\mathrm{2K_2CrO_4+H_2SO_4\rightarrow K_2Cr_2O_7+K_2SO_4+H_2O}$, so B is $\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - IList - II
(A) Bronze(I) Cu, Ni
(B) Brass(II) Fe, Cr, Ni, C
(C) UK silver coin(III) Cu, Zn
(D) Stainless steel(IV) Cu, Sn
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Bronze is copper with tin (IV); brass is copper with zinc (III).
UK "silver" coins are cupronickel, copper with nickel (I).
Stainless steel is iron with chromium, nickel and carbon (II).

questions.text:
Identify the coordination complexes in which the central metal ion has $\mathrm{d^4}$ configuration.
(A) $\mathrm{[FeO_4]^{2-}}$
(B) $\mathrm{[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}}$
(C) $\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}}$
(D) $\mathrm{Cr_2(O-\overset{O}{\overset{\Vert}{C}}-Me)_4(H_2O)_2}$
(E) $\mathrm{[NiF_6]^{2-}}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
(A) Fe(+6): $\mathrm{d^2}$.
(B) Mn(+3): $\mathrm{d^4}$.
(C) Fe(+3): $\mathrm{d^5}$.
(D) chromium(II) acetate, Cr(+2): $\mathrm{d^4}$.
(E) Ni(+4): $\mathrm{d^6}$.
So (B) and (D) only.

questions.text: Identify A, B and C in the given below reaction sequence
questions.sol:
Lead sulphide dissolves in nitric acid to give $\mathrm{Pb(NO_3)_2}$, so A is PbS (in salt analysis, PbS is the group II precipitate that is dissolved in $\mathrm{HNO_3}$).
Dilute $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ precipitates white $\mathrm{PbSO_4}$ (B).
$\mathrm{PbSO_4}$ dissolves in ammonium acetate; after acidifying with acetic acid, $\mathrm{K_2CrO_4}$ gives yellow $\mathrm{PbCrO_4}$ (C).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Consider the following reaction
Statement (I) : In the case of formaldehyde ($\mathrm{H{-}\overset{O}{\overset{\Vert}{C}}{-}H}$), K is about 2280, due to small substituents, hydration is faster.
Statement (II) : In the case of trichloro acetaldehyde ($\mathrm{H{-}\overset{O}{\overset{\Vert}{C}}{-}CCl_3}$), K is about 2000 due to $-$I effect of $-$Cl.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
For hydration $\mathrm{R_2C=O+H_2O\rightleftharpoons R_2C(OH)_2}$, small substituents (less crowding in the hydrate) and electron-withdrawing groups (a more electrophilic carbonyl carbon) favour the hydrate.
Formaldehyde has only H atoms: K is large (about $2\times10^3$). Statement I is true.
In chloral the strong $-$I effect of the three Cl atoms makes the carbonyl carbon very electrophilic: K is also large (about $2\times10^3$; chloral hydrate is a stable solid). Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Each isomer has a C=C at the ring fusion and one more C=C; ozonolysis cuts both and opens the bicyclic skeleton into one chain with four C=O groups.
(A) ring C=C next to the fusion, methyl on the five-membered ring: $\mathrm{OHC{-}CH_2CH_2{-}CO{-}CH_2{-}CH(CH_3){-}CH_2{-}CO{-}CHO}$ (III).
(B) methyl on the five-ring C=C: $\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}CH_2{-}CO{-}(CH_2)_4{-}CO{-}CHO}$ (IV).
(C) methyl on the six-membered ring next to its C=C: $\mathrm{OHC{-}CH(CH_3){-}CH_2{-}CO{-}(CH_2)_3{-}CO{-}CHO}$ (I).
(D) methyl on the five-ring C=C next to the fusion: $\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}CO{-}(CH_2)_4{-}CO{-}CH_2{-}CHO}$ (II).
Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The ascending order of relative rate of solvolysis of following compounds is :
questions.sol:
Solvolysis goes by the $\mathrm{S_N1}$ route, so the rate follows carbocation stability.
(D) gives a simple secondary alkyl cation: slowest.
(A) gives a tertiary cation.
(B) gives a secondary benzylic cation, stabilised by the fused benzene ring: faster than (A).
(C) gives the diphenylmethyl cation, stabilised by two benzene rings: fastest.
Order: (D) < (A) < (B) < (C).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Identify the products [A] and [B], respectively in the following reaction :
questions.sol:
Dow's process: chlorobenzene with NaOH at 623 K and 300 atm gives sodium phenoxide, and acidification gives phenol, so [A] is phenol.
Phenol is oxidised by acidified sodium dichromate to benzoquinone, so [B] is p-benzoquinone.
This is the option showing phenol and benzoquinone.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : The boiling points of alcohols and phenols increase with increase in the number of C-atoms.
Statement (II) : The boiling points of alcohols and phenols are higher in comparison to other class of compounds such as ethers, haloalkanes.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Boiling points rise with the number of carbon atoms because van der Waals forces increase: Statement I is true.
Intermolecular hydrogen bonding gives alcohols and phenols higher boiling points than ethers and haloalkanes of similar mass: Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The $\alpha$ - Helix and $\beta$ - Pleated sheet structures of protein are associated with its :
questions.sol:
The secondary structure of a protein is the shape the polypeptide chain takes through hydrogen bonds between $\mathrm{C=O}$ and $\mathrm{N{-}H}$ groups of the backbone.
Its two common forms are the $\alpha$-helix and the $\beta$-pleated sheet.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
When 81.0 g of aluminium is allowed to react with 128.0 g of oxygen gas, the mass of aluminium oxide produced in grams is __________. (Nearest integer)
Given :
Molar mass of Al is 27.0 g mol$^{-1}$
Molar mass of O is 16.0 g mol$^{-1}$
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{4Al+3O_2\rightarrow2Al_2O_3}$.
Al: $\dfrac{81}{27}=3$ mol; $\mathrm{O_2}$: $\dfrac{128}{32}=4$ mol. 3 mol Al needs only 2.25 mol $\mathrm{O_2}$, so Al is limiting.
$\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$ formed $=1.5$ mol $\times102$ g mol$^{-1}=153$ g.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The bond dissociation enthalpy of $\mathrm{X_2}$ $\Delta H^\circ_{\text{bond}}$ calculated from the given data is __________ kJ mol$^{-1}$. (Nearest integer)
$\mathrm{M^+X^-(s)\rightarrow M^+(g)+X^-(g)}$ $\Delta H^\circ_{\text{lattice}}=800$ kJ mol$^{-1}$
$\mathrm{M(s)\rightarrow M(g)}$ $\Delta H^\circ_{\text{sub}}=100$ kJ mol$^{-1}$
$\mathrm{M(g)\rightarrow M^+(g)+e^-(g)}$ $\Delta H^\circ_i=500$ kJ mol$^{-1}$
$\mathrm{X(g)+e^-(g)\rightarrow X^-(g)}$ $\Delta H^\circ_{\text{eg}}=-300$ kJ mol$^{-1}$
$\mathrm{M(s)+\dfrac12X_2(g)\rightarrow M^+X^-(s)}$ $\Delta H^\circ_f=-400$ kJ mol$^{-1}$
[Given : $\mathrm{M^+X^-}$ is a pure ionic compound and X forms a diatomic molecule $\mathrm{X_2}$ in gaseous state]
questions.sol:
Born-Haber cycle: $\Delta H^\circ_f=\Delta H^\circ_{\text{sub}}+\Delta H^\circ_i+\dfrac12\Delta H^\circ_{\text{bond}}+\Delta H^\circ_{\text{eg}}-\Delta H^\circ_{\text{lattice}}$.
$-400=100+500+\dfrac12\Delta H^\circ_{\text{bond}}-300-800$.
$\dfrac12\Delta H^\circ_{\text{bond}}=100 \Rightarrow \Delta H^\circ_{\text{bond}}=200$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: 0.01 mole of an organic compound (X) containing 10% hydrogen, on complete combustion produced 0.9 g $\mathrm{H_2O}$. Molar mass of (X) is __________ g mol$^{-1}$.
questions.sol:
$0.9$ g $\mathrm{H_2O}=0.05$ mol, containing $0.1$ mol H $=0.1$ g H.
So 0.01 mol of X contains 0.1 g H, i.e. 10 g H per mole.
H is 10% by mass, so the molar mass is $\dfrac{10}{0.10}=100$ g mol$^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text:
A compound 'X' absorbs 2 moles of hydrogen and 'X' upon oxidation with $\mathrm{KMnO_4|H^+}$ gives
$\mathrm{CH_3-\underset{\underset{O}{\Vert}}{C}-CH_3}$, $\mathrm{CH_3-\underset{\underset{O}{\Vert}}{C}-OH}$ and $\mathrm{CH_3-\underset{\underset{O}{\Vert}}{C}-CH_2CH_2-\underset{\underset{O}{\Vert}}{C}-OH}$.
The total number of $\sigma$ bonds present in the compound 'X' is __________.
questions.sol:
Two C=C bonds are cleaved. Acetone comes from $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C=}$, acetic acid from $\mathrm{=CH{-}CH_3}$, and the keto acid $\mathrm{CH_3CO(CH_2)_2COOH}$ is the middle piece.
X is $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C=C(CH_3){-}CH_2CH_2{-}CH=CH{-}CH_3}$, i.e. $\mathrm{C_{10}H_{18}}$.
$\sigma$ bonds: 9 C-C (an acyclic skeleton of 10 carbons has 9 carbon-carbon links, each with one $\sigma$ bond) $+$ 18 C-H $=27$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following sequence of reactions.
Total number of $\mathrm{sp^3}$ hybridised carbon atoms in the major product C formed is __________.
questions.sol:
4-Ethoxyaniline gives the diazonium salt A with $\mathrm{NaNO_2}$/HCl at 0-5$^\circ$C.
Coupling with phenol in NaOH gives B, $\mathrm{EtO{-}C_6H_4{-}N=N{-}C_6H_4{-}OH}$ ($\mathrm{C_{14}H_{14}N_2O_2}$).
NaOH and ethyl bromide convert the OH into OEt: C is $\mathrm{EtO{-}C_6H_4{-}N=N{-}C_6H_4{-}OEt}$ ($\mathrm{C_{16}H_{18}N_2O_2}$).
The only $\mathrm{sp^3}$ carbons are those of the two ethyl groups: 4.
questions.subject: Chemistry
